extracted.intended_audience: health researchers, journal editors, peer reviewers, guideline developers
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and apply appropriate reporting guidelines when planning, conducting, writing, and peer-reviewing health research to improve transparency, accuracy, and value of published work. The page catalogs principal reporting guidelines by study type (e.g., CONSORT for randomised trials, PRISMA for systematic reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: EQUATOR Network purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The EQUATOR Network seeks to improve the reliability and value of published health research literature by promoting transparent and accurate reporting and wider use of robust reporting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the first coordinated attempt to tackle the problems of inadequate reporting systematically and on a global scale; it advances the work done by individual groups over the last 15 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed with 'Extensions' (i.e., CONSORT main guideline plus extension documents for specific trial types or reporting elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed with 'Extensions' (STROBE main guideline plus extensions for particular observational designs or elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed with 'Extensions' (PRISMA main guideline and various extensions, e.g., for different review types or reporting components).

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPIRIT provides reporting guidance for study protocols (listed alongside PRISMA-P).

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-P
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA-P is included as the PRISMA extension/variant aimed at protocol reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STARD covers reporting standards for diagnostic accuracy studies (listed alongside TRIPOD).

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRIPOD provides reporting guidance for prediction model development and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CARE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed with 'Extensions' (CARE main guideline plus extensions for specific report types or fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: AGREE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGREE is listed as a standard for reporting and evaluating clinical practice guidelines (presented alongside RIGHT).

rubrics_metrics.name: RIGHT
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIGHT complements AGREE as a reporting tool for practice guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRQR
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRQR is included with COREQ as guidance for reporting qualitative research studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: COREQ
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COREQ is a 32-item checklist for interviews and focus groups reporting (listed alongside SRQR).

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE provides reporting standards for animal research (pre-clinical studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: SQUIRE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed with 'Extensions' (SQUIRE main guideline and extensions relevant to quality improvement reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHEERS provides reporting guidance for economic evaluations and is listed with 'Extensions'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guideline concept (implicit definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting guidelines are tools to promote transparent and accurate reporting of health research to improve reliability and value of published literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site links to a 'What is a reporting guideline?' resource; the surrounding text emphasizes systematic, global coordination to address inadequate reporting and encourages wider use of robust guidelines.
